description: Single-panel strain rate–temperature (processing/mechanism) map for an Fe–8% Al ferritic steel. The x-axis is linear temperature from 850 to 1150 °C with 50 °C ticks; the y-axis is logarithmic strain rate (s⁻¹) spanning 100 down to 0.01, with major gridlines at 100, 10, 1, 0.1 and 0.01 plus dense minor gridlines. Experimental data are filled circles plotted at only three temperatures — 900, 1000 and 1100 °C — each forming a vertical column of roughly eight markers distributed between about 0.1 and 10 s⁻¹. The legend on the right assigns green circles to "DDRX not activated" and red circles to "DDRX activated". Red markers always occupy the top of each column; green markers only the bottom, at or below about 1 s⁻¹. A single heavy dashed line separates the two populations, descending monotonically from roughly 2–3 s⁻¹ at 900 °C to near 0.1–0.2 s⁻¹ at 1100 °C, and continuing toward ~0.1 s⁻¹ at 1150 °C. No numeric values are printed on individual data points, so marker strain rates are readable only against the log gridlines. The map demonstrates that the DDRX-activated domain lies above the dashed boundary and expands as temperature rises, i.e. DDRX requires high temperature together with a strain rate above a temperature-dependent threshold.

subfigures.description: Strain rate (s⁻¹, log, 0.01–100) versus temperature (900–1100 °C) scatter map with three vertical columns of circular markers colour-coded red (DDRX activated) and green (DDRX not activated), separated by a descending heavy dashed boundary line; legend at right.

observations.observation: The figure is a single scatter map with the y-axis labelled 'Strain rate (s⁻¹)' on a logarithmic scale and the x-axis labelled 'Temperature (°C)'.
The strain-rate axis spans 0.01 to 100 s⁻¹ with labelled major gridlines at 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 and 100; the temperature axis spans 850 to 1150 °C with ticks every 50 °C.
Markers are plotted at only three temperatures: 900, 1000 and 1100 °C, each forming a vertical column of approximately eight circles.
The legend defines green filled circles as 'DDRX not activated' and red filled circles as 'DDRX activated'.
Within every temperature column the red (DDRX activated) markers lie at higher strain rates and the green (DDRX not activated) markers at the lowest strain rates, near or below the 1 s⁻¹ gridline.

A heavy dashed line separates the red and green populations, decreasing monotonically with increasing temperature from roughly the 2–3 s⁻¹ level at 900 °C to close to 0.1–0.2 s⁻¹ at 1100 °C and extrapolating near 0.1 s⁻¹ at 1150 °C.
No numeric values are printed next to any data point, so individual marker strain rates can only be read against the logarithmic gridlines.
The caption states that the figure is a strain rate–temperature map displaying the activation domain of the DDRX mechanism in the Fe–8% Al ferritic steel.
The citing text states that a transition occurs between the CDRX mechanism and the DDRX mechanism, with DDRX at high temperature and high strain rate and CDRX at lower temperature and strain rate.
The citing text asserts a competition between the two mechanisms as a function of deformation conditions, which the figure supports by locating the DDRX field only above the dashed boundary.
The lowest green marker in the 1100 °C column sits essentially on the 0.1 s⁻¹ gridline, marking the lower strain-rate limit of the mapped DDRX domain at the highest test temperature.
The figure contains no micrographs or text annotations other than the two legend entries and the axis labels.

unreadable_items: No numeric labels on the individual data points, so the exact strain rate of each marker cannot be read, only its position relative to the logarithmic gridlines
The criterion used to classify each point as 'DDRX activated' versus 'DDRX not activated' is not stated on the figure
The figure itself labels only DDRX activated/not activated; that the green domain corresponds to CDRX is stated in the citing text, not printed on the plot
